title: Gemma 2: Improving Open Language Models at a Practical Size
data_curation: Pre-training uses primarily-English data from web documents, code, and science articles: the 27B model trains on 13T tokens, 9B on 8T, and 2B on 2T. The same SentencePiece tokenizer as Gemma 1/Gemini is reused (256k vocab, split digits, byte-level). Filtering reuses Gemma 1 techniques: reduce unsafe utterances, strip personal/sensitive data, decontaminate evaluation sets, and minimize recitation. Post-training data extends Gemma 1.1's with internal and external public data; only the prompts (not answers) from LMSYS-chat-1M are used. Synthetic data passes multiple filtering stages removing personal information, unsafe/toxic outputs, mistaken self-identification, and duplicates; subsets that encourage in-context attribution, hedging, and refusals are added to improve factuality without hurting other metrics. The final data mixtures and hyperparameters were selected by ablations similar to Gemini 1.0.
curriculum: Post-training proceeds SFT -> RLHF -> model merging. SFT performs behavioral cloning on synthetic and real prompts with responses predominantly teacher-generated, plus on-policy distillation from the teacher on the student's own distribution. RLHF reuses the Gemma 1.1 algorithm but a new reward model about an order of magnitude larger than the policy and oriented toward multi-turn conversation, trained on labeled English-only preference data over the same SFT prompts. Finally, checkpoints from different hyperparameter runs are weight-averaged (model merging) to lift overall performance. Pre-training differs by size: the 2B and 9B students are distilled from a larger teacher (27B) rather than trained from scratch, while 27B is trained from scratch. Rationale is to improve helpfulness while minimizing safety and hallucination harms.
method: The core contribution is using knowledge distillation as the pre-training objective for the 2B and 9B models, replacing one-hot next-token prediction with the teacher's full next-token distribution. The objective minimizes the cross-entropy between teacher P_T(x|x_c) and student P_S, i.e. -sum_x P_T log P_S. Students train on more than 50x the compute-optimal token count to simulate training beyond available data. Ablations show a 2B model trained on 500B tokens with a 7B teacher reaches 67.7 vs 60.3 from scratch (500B is 10x compute-optimal). Architectural methods include interleaved local sliding-window (4096) and global (8192) attention, Grouped-Query Attention, logit soft-capping (50.0 in attention, 30.0 final), and RMSNorm pre/post-norm. Post-training combines SFT with on-policy distillation, RLHF with a large multi-turn reward model, and weight averaging of phase checkpoints.
eval_metrics: Automated benchmarks include MMLU, GSM8K, ARC-c/e, HellaSwag, Winogrande, AGIEval, DROP, BBH, MATH, HumanEval, MBPP, PIQA, SIQA, Boolq, TriviaQA, and NQ. Human evaluations cover LMSYS Chatbot Arena Elo, side-by-side safety and instruction-following win rates vs GPT-4o, and 500-scenario multi-turn ratings (1-5, avg 8.4 turns). Headline Chatbot Arena Elo: Gemma 2 27B-IT 1218 beats Llama-3 70B-IT 1206; 9B-IT 1187 matches GPT-4-0314 1186; 2.6B-IT 1126 beats GPT-3.5-Turbo-0613 1116. Pre-trained 27B scores MMLU 75.2 and GSM8K 74.0, competitive with Qwen1.5 32B and within a few points of LLaMA-3 70B. Memorization (verbatim and approximate, below 0.1%) and safety benchmarks (RealToxicity, TruthfulQA, BBQ, CrowS-Pairs, Winobias) are also reported.
key_results: Gemma 2 27B-IT reaches LMSYS Chatbot Arena Elo 1218, beating Llama-3 70B-IT (1206); 9B-IT Elo 1187 matches GPT-4-0314, and 2.6B-IT (1126) beats GPT-3.5-Turbo-0613. Distillation lifts a 2B model from 60.3 to 67.7 average on 3 benchmarks when distilled from a 7B teacher over 500B tokens.
evolution_note: Builds on the knowledge-distillation tradition (Hinton 2015) and Gemini 1.5's distillation, repurposing it as a pre-training substitute for next-token prediction to push small models far past compute-optimal token counts, reacting to Llama-3/Qwen scaling trends. In the 2024 small-model wave it helps motivate teacher-distilled pre-training and weight-averaged RLHF recipes that later open models increasingly adopt.
